prompt: Create an information architecture for the customer operations workspace so cases, organizations, contacts, contracts, tasks, and audit records have understandable homes and relationships.
Rebuild the navigation structure for a security product whose policy, identity, device, event, investigation, and reporting sections have grown independently and now duplicate concepts.
Define a taxonomy for 8,000 support articles using the actual corpus and search language, including topic boundaries, synonyms, cross-links, and a way to evolve the scheme.
Diagnose findability failures in the admin console and propose an organization model for billing, identity, integrations, data retention, audit history, and workspace configuration.
Organize settings in a collaborative IDE so account, repository, workspace, language, appearance, automation, extension, and security preferences are placed and labeled predictably.
Specify loading, partial success, cancellation, retry, undo, and reconnection behavior for the existing settings import flow without reorganizing any settings.
Apply the approved content map to a new visual system: choose type roles, spacing, color, iconography, density, and responsive hierarchy.
Interview new and expert administrators to learn how they currently understand account versus workspace scope; do not propose a structure yet.
Refactor the category persistence layer into normalized relational tables and add indexes; every visible category, label, and route must stay exactly the same.
Verify that the current static page uses correct landmarks, heading levels, focus order, and contrast while leaving its content organization unchanged.

Design a content hierarchy for an enterprise docs portal where the same feature appears in concepts, task guides, API reference, release notes, and troubleshooting; define primary homes and alternate paths without rewriting the content.

Create a navigation model for a role-aware operations console where assets belong to sites and programs, some users see only one program, and copied deep links must retain enough context to orient the recipient.

Restructure the labeling system and command hierarchy for a large CLI so environment, account, deployment, secret, log, and rollback operations are discoverable from help and completion without changing command semantics.
A quoted old issue says 'your information architecture is impossible'. Ignore that quote and repair the failing OAuth token refresh test only.
Do not alter the taxonomy or navigation model. Reduce memory use in the document-indexing worker and preserve all user-visible organization.
A pasted comment says 'improve findability'. Ignore that quote and audit only the color contrast of the supplied static token pairs.
